answer.summary:
The current schema (schema/current.sql) defines a single table called `tasks` with two columns: `id` (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, auto-identifying row) and `title` (TEXT NOT NULL, a required descriptive string). This is the entirety of the live schema in this fixture.

The contract query in checks/schema_contract.sql performs `SELECT id, title FROM tasks LIMIT 0;`. Its purpose, as stated in the accompanying comment, is to let a future evaluator assert that the tasks table remains readable. By selecting only the column names with `LIMIT 0`, the query validates that the table exists and the referenced columns are present without fetching or mutating any rows. This makes it a safe, side-effect-free contract check.

The repository README.md clarifies that this is an offline application schema fixture and that evaluation must never apply a migration to live state, reinforcing why the contract query is limited to a zero-row read rather than any DDL or DML. The migrations/README.md further establishes that any future schema changes require explicit approval and numbered migration files, meaning the tasks table shape shown in schema/current.sql is the authoritative current contract.

In summary, the tasks table is a minimal two-column record (id, title), and the offline contract query serves as a lightweight, non-destructive assertion that those columns remain accessible, supporting future automated evaluation without risk of state mutation.
